papers.title: RobPiCFM: A Training-Free Target-Conditioned Method with Foundation Models for Robotic Picking in Clutter
papers.summary: Picking objects from clutter remains a challenging problem in robotic manipulation, as it requires connecting object-level perception, grasp generation, collision-aware selection, and robot motion execution in unstructured scenes. In this paper, we present RobPiCFM, an open-source, trainingfree method for target-conditioned picking in cluttered scenes. The proposed method combines pretrained foundation-modelbased perception with RGB-D geometry, 6D object pose estimation and tracking, grasp candidate generation, constraintbased grasp filtering, and motion planning. papers.title: Time-Inhomogeneity in Risk Averse Objectives for Financial Applications of Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: In finance, sequential decision problems are often faced, for which reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a promising tool for optimisation without the need of analytical tractability. However, the objective of classical RL is the expected cumulated reward, while financial applications typically require a trade-off between return and risk. In this work, we focus on settings where one cares about the time split of the total return, ruling out most risk-aware generalisations of RL which optimise a risk measure defined on the latter. papers.title: Reinforcement Learning in Recommender Systems for Personalized Financial Decision Support: A Systematic Mapping Study
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) and bandit-based methods enable recommender systems to adapt to user and environmental feedback, offering opportunities for personalized financial decision support. However, evidence concerning their methodological integration, decision formulation, and evaluation remains fragmented across application domains. This systematic mapping study examines empirical RL-enabled recommender systems across four dimensions: RL approach, integration role, decision formulation, and evaluation practices. papers.title: Where General IT Governance Standards Fall Short for Robotic Process Automation: Content Validation and Practitioner Appraisal of an Integrated Governance Framework in UAE Telecommunications
papers.summary: Robotic process automation (RPA) is quick to deploy but difficult to govern: software robots hold privileged credentials and process customer data unattended, yet COBIT 2019, ITIL 4, ISO/IEC 38500, and TOGAF predate RPA and treat automation as an output of IT processes rather than as an actor to govern. This study derives an RPA governance framework from those four standards for UAE telecommunications and reports the evidence obtained so far. papers.title: Deep-Reinforcement-Learning-Based Dynamic Navigation for a Mecanum-Wheeled Mobile Robot
papers.summary: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a key technology to solve navigation tasks of an autonomous mobile robot (AMR) in dynamic environments due to its adaptability to complex decision-making problems. This study aims to develop a DRL method for the dynamic navigation of a Mecanum-wheel AMR. papers.title: Biologically Inspired Selective Attention for Prostate MRI: A Segmentation-Guided Vision Transformer Framework for Computer-Aided Diagnosis
papers.summary: Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men, yet interpretation of multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) suffers from substantial inter-observer variability and depends on scarce expert radiologists. Expert readers follow a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine visual strategy: they first localize the prostate gland and then direct focused attention to tissue within it. papers.title: Risk-Controlled Applicability Set Retrieval for Regulation-Grounded Construction-Site Visual Screening
papers.summary: Screening construction-site photographs against safety regulations requires two decisions: which provisions apply to what is visible, and whether each is met. Passing a fixed number of relevance-ranked provisions to a judging model misses many recorded violations; widening the list causes false alarms on inapplicable provisions. papers.summary: Background: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and accurate analysis of pulmonary abnormalities on computed tomography (CT) images is important for supporting timely diagnosis. papers.title: Velocity- and Regime-Aware Detection of Intraday Options Market Manipulation, with Explainable Attribution
papers.summary: Intraday market manipulation is hard to detect because its footprint is brief, buried in millions of quotes, and statistically similar to ordinary volatility. Detectors reach high recall only by flagging so many other days that measured precision collapses, producing alerts no regulator can act on.
